facts.title: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia
facts.text: Nearly three centuries of Armenian sovereignty, on the shores of the Mediterranean and in the heart of the Taurus.

facts.title: Ruben defies Byzantium
facts.text: He revolted against Byzantium and laid the foundations of an independent principality.

facts.title: January 6, 1198
facts.text: In the cathedral of Tarsus, Leo II was crowned the first king of Cilician Armenia, under the name Leo I.

facts.title: Meeting Möngke Khan
facts.text: Facing the Mongols, Hethum I chose to negotiate. The agreement guaranteed the integrity of the kingdom.

facts.title: Visited by Marco Polo
facts.text: Frequented by Italian merchants, Ayas made the kingdom the nerve center of trade between East and West.

facts.title: Sis falls
facts.text: The kingdom succumbed to the Mamluks. The last king, Leo VI of Lusignan, died in exile in Paris in 1393.

facts.title: The Cilician lion
facts.text: It is on the coat of arms of the Republic of Armenia. The Catholicosate of Cilicia remains in Antelias, Lebanon.

ytTitle: The Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, nearly 300 years on the Mediterranean
ytLead: From 1080 to 1375, the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, or Lesser Armenia, embodied Armenian sovereignty on the Mediterranean: the coronation of Leo I in 1198, the agreement with the Mongols, the port of Ayas visited by Marco Polo.
